launch.title: Minecraft GUI Builder
launch.question: What type of GUI do you want to create?

help.how_to_work_text: 1) Choose project type: New screen or Overlay to add elements to an existing GUI (main menu, pause, inventory...). 2) Drag components to canvas. 3) Set events and actions (Logic, Node graph). 4) Try with Preview. 5) Generate Java, or Link mod + Write to mod.
help.shortcuts_text:
Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y   undo / redo
Ctrl+C / Ctrl+V   copy / paste
Ctrl+D            duplicate
Ctrl+S            save (desktop app)
Del              delete
Arrows           move by 1 px
Shift+click      multi-selection
Double click in graph   search node
Shift+click on a texture   edit pixels
Ctrl+K            command palette
Ctrl+G / Ctrl+Shift+G   group / ungroup
Ctrl+] / Ctrl+[   bring to front / send to back
Shift+arrows     move by 10 px
Ctrl+scroll       zoom · Space+drag or middle button: pan
help.multiple_screens_text: At the top of the canvas there are screen tabs: click to switch between screens, double click to rename, ＋ to add more. To link them: select a button, set action open_gui and as target the class name of the other screen (suggested). In Preview the button really opens the other screen and close_gui goes back. In game, Esc returns to the previous screen.
help.overlay_text: The red dot on canvas is the anchor: positions in Java are relative to that point, so they follow the window. Dashed lines are an approximate reference of the vanilla GUI.
